title: Telemetry-driven calibration service for per-batch activation rescale and kernel autoplug
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a telemetry-driven calibration-as-a-service that computes per-model and per-batch activation rescale factors, exposes a policy engine for runtime kernel autoplugging, and provides safe rollback/guardrails for production rollouts. The service will take streaming model telemetry (activation histograms, KV-cache hit ratios, sequence-length distribution, latency P50/P95) and emit: 1) calibrated per-layer/per-channel scale profiles for INT8 runtime, 2) per-workload runtime hints (preferred microkernel, fused-op flag, KV prefetch config), and 3) confidence scores plus suggested fallback chains. This ticket covers design, an initial prototype service, integration points with the serving runtime, and end-to-end golden-corpus validation harnesses.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype service ingests activation histograms from runtime agents and stores time-series snapshots
Calibration output format (CSV/JSON) accepted by runtime loader and validated in unit tests
Runtime can query policy endpoint and switch kernel implementations for a request path without restart
Golden-corpus regression tests show accuracy degradation <= 0.8% vs FP32 for target models after INT8 rescale applied
Canary rollout infra and automated rollback trigger implemented (latency or quality regression thresholds)
Operational dashboard with per-model calibration drift alarms and top-3 suggested actions
risk_assessment: Medium risk: changes touch runtime kernel selection and quant scales at inference time. Primary risks are subtle accuracy regressions on long-tail prompts and transient latency spikes when switching kernels. Mitigations include staged canary, golden-corpus checks, and a conservative fallback chain that always preserves FP32 path for high-confidence failures.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scale file parser and schema validation
Integration test: runtime agent -> calib service -> runtime kernel switch in dev cluster
Golden-corpus regression: run 10K prompts across representative models and compare token-level logits, perplexity, and end-task metrics
Load test: simulate 1k QPS of telemetry ingestion and 200 concurrent policy queries
Chaos test: forced kernel unavailability and verify automatic fallback execution
implementation_notes: Telemetry format: compacted activation histograms (buckets) + sequence-length percentiles to keep payloads <2KB per request
Calibration engine: offline curve-fit per-channel rescale followed by global smoothing to avoid per-batch jitter
Policy engine: lightweight decision table with thresholds for latency, accuracy confidence, and memory pressure to choose kernel variant
Runtime handshake: non-blocking RPC to policy endpoint with a 10ms soft timeout; missing response -> use last-known policy
Fallback chain: (1) prefer quantized fused kernel, (2) fall back to quantized non-fused, (3) fall back to mixed-precision microkernel, (4) fall back to FP32

open_questions: How often should recalibration run for warm models with stable traffic? (threshold-based vs time-based)
What are the acceptable confidence thresholds to automatically promote a calibration to "production"?
Do we need signed calibration artifacts to avoid tampering in shared dedicated environments?
Should the service return per-request explanations (reason codes) for kernel choices for observability?
decisions: Prefer histogram bucketing with logarithmic bins to capture activation tail behavior
Use a conservative production promotion policy: require two consecutive canary windows with no regressions before global rollout
Expose policy metrics via existing runtime tracing framework for SLO correlation
